COMMONWEALTH OF PENNSYLVANIA
Department of Transportation Harrisburg July 16, 1973
Dauphin County 6 City of Harrisburg Pann Susquehanna Urban Renewal Project Draft Environmental Impact Statement
RECEIVED
Louis E. Keefer, Director, Bureau of Advance Planning DEPT. OF TOWNSON TATION 915 Transportation & Safety Building
JUL 1 : 1973
FROM:
TO:
Robert L. Keller, P.E., District Engineer, District 8-0/17/ANCE PLANNING PP-AJP
L. M. Filler
We have reviewed the Draft Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) for the Penn Susquehanna Urban Renewal Project in the City of Harrisburg per your request of July 3, 1973. The EIS is enclosed as requested.
The proposed Urban Renewal Project will have a negligible impact on the existing highway facilities in the project area. There are no planned highway projects.
However, we would like to offer some specific comments in regards to the EIS. These comments are:
1. On page 17, santian II.5.a, the EIS states that "a short portion of Maclay Street is included in the highway system. It is one way north." Please note that all Maclay Street is included in the highway system. Maclay Street is two-way, eastwest with the traffic signals at Front and Second Streets.
2. On page 18, section II.5.b, it states that "Elderly people also prefer this area (neighborhood #2) because it is within walking distance of downtown shopping areas." Since this neighborhood is 12 to 15 blocks from the Central Business District, the validity of this statement is in question. Certainly, the elderly may prefer this neighborhood because it is a short distance by bus to the downtown shopping areas, but not because "it is within walking distance."
3. On page 43, section II.10.a, the percentage breakdown of the natural resources used by PP&L to produce electricity adds to 104%. .
